title: Parking minimums add roughly $70,000 to the cost of a two-bedroom apartment in Sydney, $62,000 in Melbourne and up to $137,000 in Perth
oneLiner: Grattan's 2026 estimates of what the rules add to each new apartment.
body: Basement and podium parking is among the most expensive floor space in a building, and the requirement often forces an extra basement level. Grattan's May 2026 report put the cost of mandated parking at about $70,000 per two-bedroom apartment in Sydney, $62,000 in Melbourne, $113,000 in Brisbane, $95,000 in Adelaide and $137,000 in Perth, recovered in the price of every apartment including those bought by people without cars.
contextBackground: The cost claim is the economic core of the case against minimums. The 2026 figures gave it numbers that governments now quote: Victoria cited Grattan's $70,000 when it changed its rules.
contextDisagreement: The magnitude is broadly agreed. Whether removing the requirement lowers prices or raises developer margins is the live question, and depends on local competition.

evidenceItems.citation: Grattan Institute, Wasted space: Axe car-parking rules to ease the housing crisis, May 2026
Donald Shoup, The High Cost of Free Parking — construction cost of structured parking

otherClaim.title: Councils should abolish minimum parking requirements for new housing

claimItself.title: Councils should abolish minimum parking requirements for new housing
claimItself.oneLiner: Whether planning schemes should stop requiring a set number of car spaces per new dwelling and let builders decide.
claimItself.body: Most Australian planning schemes require new apartments and townhouses to include a minimum number of off-street car spaces, typically one or more per dwelling. The proposal removes the minimum. Developers could still build parking; they would no longer be required to.
